chapter_title: Concerning the Nourishment of the Person, for there are Powers in it [ ... / ... ]
chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly technical and cosmological, describing the body as a purificatory mechanism (counts of seals/rulers; cleansing via voice/word/silence; expulsion and transmigration of dark powers). The only clear later material is a short hagiographic/dialogue opener in ¶1.

paragraphs.core_text: exists [ ... ] daily to the body of the person [ ... ] there are two hundred and fifty thousand seals in it [ ... ] there are another two hundred and fifty thousand rulers [ ... ] they are cleansed and purified and enter [ ... ] ⟨p.265⟩ by the voice, by the word, and by the [ ... ... ] quiet with the silence at the time when his heart [ ... ... ] of God the Father.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the opening dialogue/frame attribution: "[Once again] speaks [ ... ]" (hagiographic/compilational voice introducing the teaching).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core substrate markers: impersonal, mechanistic description of purification in the body; large enumerated totals (250,000 + 250,000) and process-language (cleansed/purified/enter) stay within the cosmic-physiological system. Mixed only because it is introduced by a formulaic frame opener ("Once again speaks ...").

paragraphs.core_text: Also, the twelve [ ... ... ] rulers that belong to the Darkness shall be swept out outside in wandering and in transmigration [ ... ... ] some of them [ ... through] this transmigration, and others among them shall be brought back.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Old teaching voice: procedural eschatological mechanics (swept out; wandering; transmigration; brought back) applied to a numbered cosmic set (twelve rulers) without exhortation, citation, or institutional application. "Darkness" functions as a cosmic domain/force.
